craft_notes: Sthāyin: raudra-bībhatsa of hunger kept; vyabhicāri raudra at hunger surviving melt. Sanskrit-first: laṃpaṭarasā RAW per UNC (kept greed-juiced, never softened); saṃhāra-nāman (DISSOLUTION-NAMED — kept as address). Rows: 9 (doubt/conduct/glory/rule — four meltings, hunger survives all), 1 (‘split part’ closes — hṛd-bheda last: the heart's split struck). Close: ‘strike my heart’s split part’. Rupture: comma (melted stated, then the feast — all gone, then hunger). Rejected: softening greed — killed: raw kept (hunger survives BECAUSE raw); ‘feast unending’ reorder — killed: endless-feast-entire kept heaped. Read aloud: DOUBT-melt-ed, CON-duct-GONE, GLO-ry-GONE, RULE-gone — … TO-gulp THE-end-LESS-feast en-TIRE, GREED-juiced, O-dis-so-LU-tion-NAMED, STRIKE my-HEART's-split-PART.

lines: Doubt melted, conduct gone, glory gone, rule gone —
to gulp the endless feast entire, greed-juiced, O dissolution-named, strike my heart's split part.
l4.sanskrit_cite: vilīne śaṅkaughe sapadi paripūrṇe ca vibhave | saṃhārākhyā mama hṛdi bhidāṃśaṃ praharatu

reads_against.argmap: What survives melting? → All melted but hunger: strike prayed.
c1_essence: Melted all but hunger; strike prayed.
